How NoteDown runs for internal tests: what is hosted where, the one-time
setup only the owner can do (accounts, DNS, keys), and how deployments
run afterwards. Everything stays within free tiers. The examples use
`notedown.example.com` for the web app and `notedown-api.example.com`
for the server — replace them with subdomains of your own domain.

## Overview

| Part | Runs on | Deployed by | HTTPS |
|---|---|---|---|
| Web app (`app/`) | GitHub Pages, `https://notedown.example.com` | `.github/workflows/web.yml` on every push to `main` that changes `app/` | Let's Encrypt, managed by GitHub |
| Sync server (`server/`) | Google Cloud Run, region `europe-west1`, `https://notedown-api.example.com` | `.github/workflows/server.yml`: tests on every push, deploy from `main` | Google-managed certificate |
| Database | Neon Postgres (free plan, Frankfurt) | schema created by the server at start | TLS (`sslmode=require`) |
| Android app (`mobile/`) | APK in the GitHub pre-release `android-test` | `.github/workflows/android.yml`: APK on every push, release from `main`, the app "NoteDown Preview" from other branches | — |

Secrets never sit in the repository: the database URL and the server's
token secret live in Google Secret Manager, the Android signing key in
the GitHub environment `release`, which only jobs running from `main`
can use (a branch build never gets it, section 5). Deploying from GitHub
to Google uses workload identity federation (short-lived tokens, no
stored key), limited to `main` of this repository. Until a step below is
done, its deploy job is skipped, not failed.

**Free-tier limits that matter:** Cloud Run 2 million requests per
month (a synced app that is open polls every 5 s with two requests — the
file list and the open invitations — about 260,000 requests a month for
a device open all working day; while nothing changes the interval grows
to 30 s, so a mostly idle device needs about 40,000), and the service is capped at 2 instances; Artifact Registry
0.5 GB (the setup keeps the 5 newest images); Neon 1 GB of data per
project (since 2026-10; the admin page measures against it,
`DATABASE_LIMIT_MB` below) and a
database that sleeps after 5 idle minutes (the first request afterwards
takes about a second; compute hours are limited on the free plan).
Google needs a billing account even within the free tier; a budget alert
guards against surprises.

## Setup order

Each step takes 5–15 minutes; steps 2–4 depend on each other, 1 and 5
don't.

0. Merge the branch with this setup into `main` (workflows only run from
   `main`).
1. Web app on GitHub Pages with the subdomain.
2. Neon database.
3. Google Cloud project, then run `scripts/setup-gcp.sh`.
4. Server subdomain on Cloud Run.
5. Android signing key.
6. Alerts by email.
7. Admin page (needs sync on in your browser).
8. TRMNL plugin (optional, needs a TRMNL account).
9. Check everything (see "Checks").

## 1. Web app on GitHub Pages

1. **Namecheap** → Domain List → *Manage* next to the domain → *Advanced
   DNS* → *Add New Record*:
   - Type `CNAME Record`, Host `notedown`, Value `sarrdai.github.io.`,
     TTL Automatic. (Namecheap adds the domain to the host by itself.)
   - Only if the domain's nameservers are not "Namecheap BasicDNS", the
     record goes to whichever DNS provider is set there.
2. **GitHub** → the repository → *Settings* → *Pages* → *Build and
   deployment* → Source: **GitHub Actions**.
3. *Settings* → *Secrets and variables* → *Actions* → *Variables* → New
   repository variable `WEB_HOST` = `notedown.example.com`.
4. *Actions* → *Web* → *Run workflow* (branch `main`).
5. *Settings* → *Pages* → *Custom domain*: `notedown.example.com` →
   Save. GitHub checks the DNS record (up to an hour), then issues the
   certificate; tick **Enforce HTTPS** as soon as it can be ticked.
   Afterwards `https://notedown.example.com` shows the app.
6. Repository variables `OPERATOR_NAME` and `OPERATOR_EMAIL` (and, if
   you want it shown, `OPERATOR_ADDRESS`, with `\n` between lines): who
   runs this copy, named in the privacy policy (`/privacy/`) and the terms
   of use (`/terms/`). The web and Android deploys write them into
   `app/config.json` (`scripts/write-config.js`), together with the
   version Settings → About shows; without them the pages say no operator
   is set. The texts describe this setup (GitHub Pages, Cloud Run in
   `europe-west1`, Neon in Frankfurt): whoever hosts elsewhere edits
   `app/privacy/index.html`. The Play Console asks for
   `https://notedown.example.com/privacy/` and, for deleting data,
   `https://notedown.example.com/delete/`.

Recommended against someone else claiming the subdomain on GitHub: your
GitHub *profile* settings → *Pages* → *Add a domain* → `example.com`; it
shows a TXT record (host `_github-pages-challenge-sarrdai`) to add in
Namecheap the same way, then *Verify*.

## 2. Neon database

1. Sign up at neon.com (GitHub login works) → *New project*: name
   `notedown`, Postgres version as offered, region **AWS Europe Central 1
   (Frankfurt)**.
2. *Connect* → turn **Connection pooling off** and copy the connection
   string (`postgresql://…neon.tech/neondb?sslmode=require…`). It is
   needed in section 3 and then never again — don't store it anywhere else.
3. The admin page shows the database size against the plan's limit,
   which the server can't ask Neon for: GitHub → *Settings* → *Secrets
   and variables* → *Actions* → *Variables* → New repository variable
   `DATABASE_LIMIT_MB` = the limit in MB (`1024` on the free plan), then
   run the *Server* workflow; change it with the plan or the host.
   Without it the server runs as usual and the admin page shows "Limit
   not set".

## 3. Google Cloud

1. console.cloud.google.com → create a project, e.g. `notedown-test`
   (note the *project ID*, it may carry a number).
2. *Billing* → link a billing account (credit card; nothing is charged
   within the free tier). *Billing* → *Budgets & alerts* → *Create
   budget*: 1 € per month, email alerts at 50 % and 100 %.
3. Open **Cloud Shell** (the `>_` icon top right), then:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/Sarrdai/NoteDown.git
   bash NoteDown/scripts/setup-gcp.sh <project-id>
   ```

   It enables the APIs, creates the image registry, two service accounts
   (one the server runs as, one GitHub deploys with), the two secrets
   (asks for the Neon connection string; generates the token secret) and
   the federation that lets only `main` of this repository deploy. It
   can be run again safely.
4. Add the three repository variables it prints (`GCP_PROJECT_ID`,
   `GCP_REGION`, `GCP_WIF_PROVIDER`) like `WEB_HOST` in step 1.
5. *Actions* → *Server* → *Run workflow* on `main`. The deploy job ends
   with a health check against the new service.

## 4. Server subdomain

Cloud Run serves a custom domain once Google knows the domain is yours.

1. In Cloud Shell: `gcloud domains verify example.com` → opens Google
   Search Console, which shows a **TXT record**. Add it in Namecheap
   (Advanced DNS → TXT Record, Host `@`, the value shown), then click
   *Verify* in Search Console (can take a few minutes).
2. In Cloud Shell:

   ```bash
   gcloud beta run domain-mappings create --service notedown-api \
     --domain notedown-api.example.com --region europe-west1
   ```

3. Namecheap → CNAME Record, Host `notedown-api`, Value
   `ghs.googlehosted.com.`.
4. Google issues the certificate within 15–60 minutes;
   `gcloud beta run domain-mappings describe --domain
   notedown-api.example.com --region europe-west1` shows the status.
5. Add the repository variable `API_HOST` = `notedown-api.example.com`:
   the web and Android deploys write it into `app/config.json`, where the
   app finds its sync server (without it, sync can't be turned on); the
   same file holds `web`, the web app's address (`WEB_HOST`), which
   invitation links start with.
   Both host variables hold the bare host name (no `https://`); the
   deploys stop with an error on a URL or the `example.com` placeholder
   (`scripts/check-host.sh`).

## 5. Android signing key

Every test build must carry the same signature, or the next one doesn't
install over the last (and uninstalling deletes the notes on the phone).
The key is created once, by you, and kept like a password.

1. In Cloud Shell (it has Java) or any computer with a JDK:

   ```bash
   keytool -genkeypair -keystore notedown-release.jks -alias notedown \
     -keyalg RSA -keysize 4096 -validity 10000 -dname "CN=NoteDown"
   base64 -w0 notedown-release.jks > notedown-release.b64
   ```

   It asks for a password (one for the keystore and the key).
2. Keep `notedown-release.jks` and the password in your password manager
   — losing them means users have to reinstall later. In Cloud Shell,
   download the file (⋮ → *Download*) and then delete both files there.
3. GitHub → *Settings* → *Environments* → *New environment* `release` →
   *Deployment branches and tags* → **Selected branches and tags** → *Add
   deployment branch or tag rule* → `main`. In that environment, *Add
   environment secret*:
   - `ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64` = content of `notedown-release.b64`,
   - `ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD` = the password.

   **Then delete the repository secrets** of the same names (*Settings* →
   *Secrets and variables* → *Actions*), if they exist: every branch's
   workflow runs can read repository secrets, including a run whose
   workflow file was changed on that branch, so anyone who can push a
   branch could read the key that signs the app. An environment secret
   with this rule goes only to jobs that run from `main`; the rule is
   what protects it, since a branch's own workflow file could name
   `release` too. The workflows pick the environment themselves: the
   Android job runs in `release` on `main` and in `preview` (which GitHub
   creates on first use) on every other branch. While the key is still a
   repository secret, each branch build says so in a warning.
4. *Actions* → *Android* → *Run workflow* on `main`.
5. **Invitation links open the app** (Android App Link): nothing to do
   by hand. The `release-key` job of the web deploy (environment
   `release`) reads the certificate fingerprint from the keystore
   (step 3) and hands only that on to the deploy job, which publishes it
   as `https://notedown.example.com/.well-known/assetlinks.json`. That is
   how Android checks that the app may open links of that host; the
   Android build takes the host from the repository variable `WEB_HOST`
   (step 1). The file exists only while the secret is set. Run *Actions*
   → *Web* → *Run workflow* once after adding the secrets (the deploy
   otherwise runs on the next change of `app/`). Until then (and in debug
   builds, which are signed with another key) an invitation link opens in
   the browser, and "Add contact" → "Paste link" takes it. Check on the
   phone after installing: `adb shell pm get-app-links
   io.github.sarrdai.notedown` shows the host as `verified`.
6. **Optional: a preview key** for branch builds. NoteDown Preview
   (see "Installing the test app") is never signed with the release
   key. Repeat the two commands of step 1 with `notedown-preview` in
   place of `notedown-release` (same alias `notedown`) and add
   `ANDROID_PREVIEW_KEYSTORE_BASE64` = the content of
   `notedown-preview.b64` and `ANDROID_PREVIEW_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD` = its
   password, as repository secrets or as secrets of the environment
   `preview`. Every branch build can read them, so the key must be good
   for nothing but previews. Without it a preview is signed with a debug
   key that is new in every build, and previews don't install over each
   other.

Without the release secrets, `main` still builds a **debug** APK (as a
workflow artifact) but publishes no release.

## 6. Alerts

Two alerts mail you when the server has a problem:

- **Server down:** an uptime check calls `/health/live` every 5 minutes
  from 3 regions (Europe, Iowa, Virginia); the alert fires when it fails
  from more than one region for 5 minutes. The endpoint doesn't touch
  the database, so Neon still sleeps when nobody uses the app.
- **Server errors:** 3 or more 5xx responses within 10 minutes — mostly
  a database that is down or unreachable, noticed as soon as the app is
  used.

After the first successful server deploy (step 3, item 5), run the script a
second time in Cloud Shell:

```bash
bash NoteDown/scripts/setup-gcp.sh <project-id>
```

Press Enter at the Neon prompt to keep the stored connection string, then
enter the email address for the alerts. Google sends the alerts from
`alerting-noreply@google.com`; check the spam folder the first time.

Cost: the check runs about 26,000 times a month (3 regions × 12 per hour)
— within the 1 million free uptime-check runs and 1.3 % of Cloud Run's 2
million free requests. Alert policies are free; Google has announced a
charge of $0.35 per month per metric in a policy from September 2027,
which would be $0.70 a month for these two. The checks keep one Cloud Run
instance warm; idle instances cost nothing with request-based billing.

## 7. Admin page

`https://notedown.example.com/admin/` is the owner's maintenance page
(`docs/requirements.md` → "Server maintenance (admin)"). It signs in with
the NoteDown device of the browser it is opened in, so open it in a
browser where the web app has sync turned on (or is linked to your
phone).

1. Open the admin page. It answers "This identity is not an admin …" and
   shows your identity ID; *Copy ID*.
2. GitHub → *Settings* → *Secrets and variables* → *Actions* →
   *Secrets* → New repository secret `ADMIN_IDENTITIES` = the ID
   (several IDs separated by commas). The ID alone opens nothing (signing
   in needs the device keys); it is a secret so the public deploy logs
   don't show which identity runs the server.
3. *Actions* → *Server* → *Run workflow* on `main`, then reload the admin
   page.

To take the access away, remove the ID from the secret and deploy
again, or remove the device from your identity.

## 8. TRMNL plugin

Optional: the plugin that shows shared notes on a TRMNL display
(`docs/requirements.md` → "TRMNL display"). It runs inside the server and
stays off until its client ID is set. TRMNL's guide:
<https://docs.trmnl.com/go/plugin-marketplace/introduction>.

1. Create a new **public plugin** at <https://trmnl.com/plugins/my/new>
   (needs TRMNL's Developer Edition; it stays unlisted until you submit
   it). Enter, with your `API_HOST`:

   | Field | Value |
   |---|---|
   | Installation URL | `https://notedown-api.example.com/trmnl/install` |
   | Installation success webhook URL | `https://notedown-api.example.com/trmnl/installed` |
   | Plugin management URL | `https://notedown-api.example.com/trmnl/manage` |
   | Plugin markup URL | `https://notedown-api.example.com/trmnl/markup` |
   | Uninstallation webhook URL | `https://notedown-api.example.com/trmnl/uninstalled` |

   Name it "NoteDown"; a supported refresh interval of 15 minutes is
   plenty for notes. Leave *No Screen Padding* off: the screen is laid
   out for TRMNL's views with their padding.
2. TRMNL then lists the plugin under *My Plugins* with a **client ID**
   (the server checks with it that the token TRMNL opens the settings
   page with is meant for this plugin; the client secret isn't needed). GitHub → *Settings* → *Secrets and variables* → *Actions* →
   *Secrets*: add `TRMNL_CLIENT_ID` (the deploy passes it on with `WEB_APP_URL` = `https://` + `WEB_HOST`,
   where the plugin's invitation links point).
3. *Actions* → *Server* → *Run workflow* on `main`.
4. Install the plugin on your TRMNL. TRMNL sends you to the server and
   back; save the instance, then open its settings with *Configure*
   (they open only from TRMNL, `docs/sync-and-sharing.md` → "TRMNL"), scan the code
   with NoteDown, share a note with the new contact TRMNL and pick what
   shows. The display picks it up with its next refresh.

To switch the plugin off, delete the secret and deploy again;
installations then get no picture until it is back.

## Installing the test app

On the Android phone: open the repository's *Releases* → **android-test**
→ download `notedown.apk` → open it and allow "install unknown apps" for
the browser when asked. Later builds install over it.

**Trying a branch** without replacing the test app: every push to another
branch that changes `app/` or `mobile/` builds **NoteDown Preview**, an app
of its own (ID `io.github.sarrdai.notedown.preview`, its own data — link it
as a further device to see your notes). *Actions* → *Android* → the branch's
run → *Artifacts* → `notedown-apk` (a ZIP: unpack it, then install
`notedown.apk`). Previews are signed with the preview key (section 5) when
it is set up, so later preview builds install over it. Without it they are
signed with a debug key that changes with every build: uninstall the
previous preview first and link the new one again (it is a linked device).
A preview installed before its own key existed was signed with the release
key and has to be uninstalled the same way, once. Invitation links keep
opening the test app.

## Checks

| What | Expected |
|---|---|
| `https://notedown.example.com` | The app opens, padlock in the address bar |
| `https://notedown-api.example.com/health` | `{"ok":true}` |
| `https://notedown.example.com/admin/` | the overview with your identity marked "You" |
| Cloud Console → *Monitoring* → *Uptime checks* → `notedown-api live` | green in all 3 regions |
| Cloud Console → *Monitoring* → *Alerting* | the policies `NoteDown server down` and `NoteDown server errors`, notifying your email |
| *Actions* → latest *Server*, *Web*, *Android* runs on `main` | green; deploy jobs not skipped |
| *Actions* → latest *Android* run of another branch | green, no warning about the release key (it would say the key is still readable by branch builds) |
| Releases → `android-test` | `notedown.apk`, build number of the latest run |

If a deploy job fails: its log names the step. Typical causes are a
missing or misspelled repository variable (deploy jobs), the Pages source
not set to GitHub Actions (web), or DNS not yet propagated (domain
checks; wait an hour).

## Day to day

- Merging into `main` deploys whatever changed: `app/` → web app and
  Android release, `server/` → server.
- Third-party actions in `.github/workflows/` are pinned by commit, with
  the version as a comment (`uses: actions/checkout@<commit>  # v7.0.1`).
  To update one, look up the commit its new tag points to (not the tag
  object of an annotated tag) and keep the version comment.
- Server logs: Cloud Console → *Cloud Run* → `notedown-api` → *Logs*.
- The database schema is created and extended by the server at start
  (`server/notedown_server/schema.sql`, only additive statements).
- **Backups:** the admin page → *Download backup* saves the whole server
  state as one file (encrypted notes and their stored older states,
  public keys, who shares with whom — keep it private anyway; version
  history makes it larger). Take one before risky changes and from time
  to time. *Restore backup…* replaces everything with such a file (up to
  32 MB, Cloud Run's request limit); devices merge their notes back in at
  their next sync, devices linked after the backup must be linked again.
  Neon's own point-in-time restore (Neon console → the project →
  *Restore*; the free plan keeps only a short history window) works too
  and is handled by the devices the same way.
- To shut everything down: delete the Google Cloud project, the Neon
  project, the Pages custom domain and the DNS records.
